---
title: Add a content type
description: Declare a content type and get the list, the form, and the routes for it.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-file-plus
---

This guide adds a content type from a layer. A backend layer must register a content adapter. For example, `@plutocms/supabase` registers a Supabase adapter. See [Content adapter](/supabase/content-adapter).

## Step 1: declare the type

Put the declaration in `shared/utils/`. Nuxt auto-imports the exports of `shared/utils/**` and `shared/types/**`.

```ts [shared/utils/content-note.ts]
export const noteType = defineContentType({
  name: 'note',
  label: 'Note',
  labelPlural: 'Notes',
  icon: 'lucide:sticky-note',
  source: 'notes',
  titleField: 'title',
  fields: [
    { name: 'title', type: 'text', label: 'Title', required: true, inList: true },
    { name: 'slug', type: 'slug', label: 'Slug', from: 'title', required: true, inList: true, region: 'side' },
    { name: 'body', type: 'textarea', label: 'Body' }
  ],
  slug: { field: 'slug' },
  status: false,
  timestamps: { created: 'created_at', updated: false },
  capabilities: { write: 'notes:manage', delete: 'notes:delete' }
})
```

- `source` is the storage name. For the Supabase adapter, it is the table name.
- `status: false` means no publish workflow.
- A type that declares no capability for an operation is open to anyone who can reach the route.

::warning
Keep the file under `shared/utils/`. A value exported from another `shared/` folder gets only a type declaration. A site that extends your layer then fails at Nitro startup.
::

## Step 2: register on the client

```ts [app/plugins/pluto-extension.ts]
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  definePlutoExtension({
    id: 'my-layer',
    contentTypes: [{ id: 'note', type: noteType }],
    capabilities: [
      { id: 'notes-manage', key: 'notes:manage', label: 'my-layer.capabilities.notesManage' },
      { id: 'notes-delete', key: 'notes:delete', label: 'my-layer.capabilities.notesDelete' }
    ]
  })
})
```

Use a plain, un-prefixed `id` for the entry. Read `type.name` for the real name of the type.

Core now adds a sidebar entry, a dashboard tile, and the pages `/admin/content/note`, `/admin/content/note/new`, and `/admin/content/note/<id>`. See [Lists and forms](/core/forms).

## Step 3: register on the server

```ts [server/plugins/content.ts]
export default defineNitroPlugin(() => {
  registerContentType(noteType)
})
```

This enables the generic routes under `/api/_pluto/content/note`. Add `hooks.afterCreate` and `hooks.afterUpdate` here when you need server work after a write.

## Step 4: add the storage

For the Supabase backend, add a migration that creates the table and grants it. The adapter maps the fields to the columns. Set `column` on a field when the column name differs from the field name.

```sql [db/migrations/002_notes.sql]
create table if not exists public.notes (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  slug text not null unique,
  title text not null,
  body text
);

alter table public.notes enable row level security;

grant select on public.notes to anon;
grant select, insert, update, delete on public.notes to authenticated;
grant select, insert, update, delete on public.notes to service_role;
```

Add RLS policies that match your capabilities. Use `public.has_capability('notes:manage')`. See [Users and roles](/supabase/users-and-roles) and [Data API grants](/supabase/grants).

## Step 5: translate the labels

Add the convention keys to the locale files of your layer. Core falls back to the English literals when a key is missing.

- `content.note.label`, `content.note.labelPlural`, `content.note.new`
- `content.note.fields.<field>.label`
- `content.note.status.<value>`

## Options for your own URLs

If your layer must keep existing admin URLs, set `autoRoutes: false` and set `basePath`, `newPath`, and `editPath`:

```ts
basePath: '/admin/notes',
newPath: '/admin/note/new',
editPath: id => `/admin/note/edit/${id}`
```

Then register nav and pages by hand and render `PlutoContentList` and `PlutoContentForm` in your page files.

If an id can hold a slash, such as a nested id of the GitHub CMS, build the edit link with `contentIdPath(id)`. It keeps the `/` between the segments.

## Custom field widgets

If a field needs its own input, see [Add a field widget](/guides/add-a-field-widget).
